title: Boundary primes and DVR localizations of a simultaneous parameter-root algebra
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a henselian Noetherian regular local ring of dimension $d$, let $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ be a regular system of parameters, let $0\leq r\leq d$, and let $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put
$$B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),\quad f=\prod_{i=1}^r t_i,$$
using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For every $1\leq i\leq r$, the rings $R/(t_i)$ and $B/(x_i)$ are regular local domains, $t_i$ and $x_i$ are nonzerodivisors, and the canonical presentation
$$B/(x_i)\cong (R/(t_i))[x_j:j\ne i]/(x_j^n-\bar t_j:j\ne i)$$
makes $B/(x_i)$ finite free over $R/(t_i)$ with the monomial basis containing $1$. In particular $\mathfrak p_i=(t_i)$ and $\mathfrak q_i=(x_i)$ are prime and $\mathfrak q_i\cap R=\mathfrak p_i$. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ [def-pc-field-extension]. The rings $V_i=R_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and $A_i=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] are discrete valuation rings with uniformizers $t_i,x_i$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and the canonical map gives an isomorphism of $V_i$-algebras
$$B\otimes_R V_i\cong A_i.$$
Thus $V_i\to A_i$ is finite and injective, induces $K\to E$ on fraction fields, and satisfies $\mathfrak m_{V_i}A_i=(t_i)=(x_i^n)=\mathfrak m_{A_i}^{n}$. Each $\mathfrak q_i$ has height one, meaning there is no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak q_i$, and these are all the height-one primes of $B$ containing $f$. For $r=0$ this list is empty and $f=1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-henselian-parameter-root-regularity] to $R,t_1,\ldots,t_d,r,n$. It gives a Noetherian regular local domain $B$, the injective finite free map $R\to B$, its monomial basis, and the regular system of parameters $x_1,\ldots,x_r,t_{r+1},\ldots,t_d$ of $B$. In particular $R$ is a domain, since it injects into the nonzero domain $B$. These conclusions allow both fraction fields in the statement to be formed. All the lemma's hypotheses are present: henselianity, Noetherian regular locality, a full parameter system, $r\leq d$, and $n>0$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root presentation; its regular-local algebra is recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: Fix $1\leq i\leq r$. Permute each of the parameter systems of $R$ and $B$ to put $t_i$ and $x_i$ first. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], each first element is a nonzerodivisor, and $R/(t_i)$ and $B/(x_i)$ are regular local rings of dimension $d-1$. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], both quotients are nonzero domains. Consequently $\mathfrak p_i=(t_i)$ and $\mathfrak q_i=(x_i)$ are proper prime ideals. The same regular-sequence assertion implies $t_i\ne0$ and $x_i\ne0$, since these rings are nonzero.

source.place: Tags 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), allowing a permutation of minimal generators, and 00NP (lemma-regular-domain).

proof.text: The presentation of $B/(x_i)$ follows directly from its generators and relations. In the quotient $x_i=0$ and $x_i^n=t_i$ force $t_i=0$, because $n>0$. Send coefficients to their classes in $R/(t_i)$, send $x_i$ to zero, and keep the other variables. In the reverse direction send coefficients and surviving variables to their classes in $B/(x_i)$. Each map respects every displayed root relation, and their composites fix all generators. This proves the claimed isomorphism, including its compatibility with $R/(t_i)$.

source.place: Explicit generators-and-relations calculation for the root presentation in IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed p.133.

proof.text: The quotient R/(t_i) is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-henselian-pair]. Permuting the full parameter list to put t_i first and applying the regular-sequence quotient theorem shows that the surviving parameters followed by the image of the tail form a full regular system. Apply [lem-sfb-henselian-parameter-root-regularity] over R/(t_i) to those surviving parameters. Transport its basis through the explicit presentation of step 3 and the equivalence between Fin(r-1) and the indices other than i. This gives exactly the displayed surviving-root monomials, including when r=1 and the index type is empty. The resulting nonempty finite basis implies faithfulness and finiteness of the coefficient algebra, and hence injectivity and finiteness of its ring homomorphism. Injectivity identifies its kernel with (t_i), giving contraction.

source.place: ILO IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed p.133: simultaneous parameter-root monomial basis applied over the henselian parameter quotient; henselian quotient descent is Stacks Tag 09XI.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-regular-principal-prime-localization-dvr] first with $H=R$, $g=t_i$, and $B=V_i$, and then with $H=B$, $g=x_i$, and localization $A_i$. The Noetherian, nonzerodivisor and principal-prime hypotheses were verified in steps 1-2. Both localizations are DVR domains. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] their maximal ideals are $\mathfrak p_iV_i=(t_i)$ and $\mathfrak q_iA_i=(x_i)$, respectively. Hence these images are uniformizers by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The fraction descriptions show that the two localization maps are injective: all denominators are nonzero in their source domains.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), principal nonzero maximal-ideal criterion, and Tag 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text: Every prime Q of B contracting to (t_i) contains x_i, since x_i^n=t_i and n>0. Thus (x_i) is contained in Q. The finite R-algebra B is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Integral incomparability [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] excludes strict containment of these primes with equal contraction, so Q=(x_i). Apply [lem-trf-unique-prime-localization] to identify the localization of B away from (t_i) with B_(x_i). The tensor-localization equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] gives B tensor_R R_(t_i) isomorphic to B_(x_i). Its maps agree with the canonical maps on B, and extensionality on R proves agreement on R_(t_i). Finite base change and tensor symmetry prove finiteness of R_(t_i) to B_(x_i); localization of the injective domain map proves injectivity.

source.place: ILO IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134, boundary localization comparison; Stacks Tags 00GT (integral incomparability), 00EA (unique-prime localization), 00DK (tensor localization).

proof.text:
Localizing a domain at nonzero denominators leaves its fraction field unchanged: a fraction of localized elements $(a/s)/(b/u)$ equals $au/(sb)$, and every original fraction is still a quotient of elements of the localized ring. Consequently $\operatorname{Frac}(V_i)=K$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(A_i)=E$. The canonical maps used above restrict to $R\to B$, so their induced field map is the canonical injection $K\to E$, $a/b\mapsto a/b$. The maximal ideals from step 5 give
$$\mathfrak m_{V_i}A_i=(t_i)A_i=(x_i^n)A_i=((x_i)A_i)^n=\mathfrak m_{A_i}^{n},$$
where the middle equalities use the defining root relation and multiplication of principal ideals.

source.place: Fraction calculations from Tag 00CO (definition-localization); the defining equation of the parameter-root presentation in IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed p.133.

proof.text: A nonzero nonunit generating a prime principal ideal in a Noetherian domain has height one, by Mathlib Ideal.height_span_singleton_eq_one_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors (KrullsHeightTheorem). Apply this to each x_i, which is regular by step 2. Conversely, if a height-one prime Q contains the boundary product, primality and the root relation give some x_i in Q, hence (x_i) is contained in Q. The equal heights force equality, by Ideal.eq_of_le_of_height_le. For r=0 the product is 1 and no prime contains it.
